title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Gray Local Media
description: The USPFO for Hawaii intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Gray Local Media (Hawaii News Now) on behalf of the Hawaii Air National Guard (HIANG) Recruiting and Retention Office for a base period of 12-months plus three 12-month options periods for digital and televised advertising campaign. This commercial service acquisition is conducted under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services), utilizing simplified procedures pursuant to RFO 12.201-1. The statutory authority which permits other than full and open competition for this acquisition is 41 U.S.C. � 1901 and RFO 12.102 (Restricting competition), as only one source is reasonably available to satisfy the agency's requirement. Period of Performance: Base period: (Estimated) September 30, 2026 � September 29, 2027; Option Period 1: (Estimated) September 30, 2027 � September 29, 2028 Option Period 2: (Estimated) September 30, 2028 � September 29, 2029 Option Period 3: (Estimated) September 30, 2029 � September 29, 2030 Intended Source: Gray Local Media (Hawaii News Now) SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION The HIANG Recruiting and Retention Office must engage its primary target demographic (physically fit young adults aged 18 to 25) for enlistment. High-visibility local sports broadcasting is the premier vehicle to reach this regional demographic. Gray Local Media (Hawaii News Now) holds the exclusive broadcasting and media distribution rights for University of Hawaii (UH) athletic events. No other media company or television network can broadcast these live games or provide corresponding digital and video advertising integrations within these specific high-traffic broadcasts. Because of this exclusivity, Gray Local Media (Hawaii News Now) is the unique source capable of placing HIANG Recruiting's digital and video advertising directly inside the televised games and related program packaging that commands the attention of the targeted local audience. Consequently, a solicitation to any other source would fail to satisfy the government's requirement for UH Athletics-centered broadcast reach. SCOPE OF WORK HIANG Recruiting and Retention is procuring digital/video advertising services to engage and recruit physically fit young adults (ages 18-25) into the HIANG. Distribution: Hawaii News Now channels (including K5) will display HIANG Recruiting digital advertising (video ads and virtual logos). Commercial Volume: A total of 691 commercials (per 12-month period) will be advertised among UH televised games. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICE HIANG Recruiting will utilize digital and video advertising showcasing and promoting various HIANG mission sets. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, any interested party that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a written capability statement illustrating its ability to provide identical services (specifically, exclusive advertising rights during televised University of Hawaii sports broadcasts). All capability statements must be submitted via email no later than 5 September 2026, at 10:00 AM HST. Submission Requirements: Company Name, UEID, and CAGE Code. Business Size under NAICS Code 516120 - Television Broadcasting Stations. Point of Contact information (Name, Phone, Email). Technical description of capability to deliver the required 691 commercials specifically within televised University of Hawaii athletic games. Documentation demonstrating equivalent media broadcasting rights for UH sports events. Submit Responses To: Contracting Specialist: Emma Newbegin via email at emma.a.newbegin.civ@army.mil A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

title: Borough of Etna, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: This is a Presolicitation Notice only. This is not a Solicitation (Request for Quote). No purchase order will be awarded from this announcement. Any applicable attachments for this project (i.e., Drawings and Specifications) will be issued at the time of the Solicitation. This procurement is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. All interested and capable small business offerors are encouraged to submit a bid/proposal. Project Description The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project that involves the rehabilitation of the Etna Federal Local Protection Project along West Little Pine Creek in the Borough of Etna and Shaler Township between station 24+00 and 26+90, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. The original channel and embankment sustained severe erosion and structural damage during storm events in April 2024. The work is to be completed within 120 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $200,000.00 and $450,000.00. Major Components of Work: Site Control & Water Management: The contractor will be responsible for the design, installation, monitoring, and removal of temporary water diversions, pumping/dewatering systems, and robust erosion/sediment control measures to maintain a dry in-channel work environment. Excavation & Channel Restoration: This phase requires the excavation, clearing, and off-site disposal of accumulated in-channel sediment, debris, failed concrete pavement, and damaged riprap. Embankment Reconstruction: The work includes sourcing, hauling, placing, and compacting approved soil fill to restore the embankment to its original design grade. Geotextile & Armoring Repair: The project requires the installation of new non-woven geotextile fabric (PennDOT Class 4, Type A) and the replacement of damaged R-4 riprap on the prepared subgrade along the left embankment. Structural Concrete & Grout Works: The contractor will be required to recast concrete-sealed stone and slope protection using PennDOT Class A Concrete, ensuring proper consolidation and bonding with the riprap matrix. Site Establishment: The project will conclude with seeding, grading, and establishing permanent vegetative cover over all disturbed areas to prevent future erosion. The contractor is responsible for all project submittals, including, but not limited to, a Quality Control Plan and Accident Prevention Plan. Special Notice: Safety and Qualification Requirements Safety Compliance (EM 385-1-1): Offerors are advised that all work on this project must strictly comply with the latest edition of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1) (Link: https://www.publications.usace.army.mil/Portals/76/EM%20385-1-1%20_EFFECTIVE%2015March2024.pdf). Prior to commencing work, the contractor must submit and secure Government approval for a site-specific Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and comprehensive Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs). To enforce these standards, the contractor must employ a full-time, dedicated Level 1 Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) who must be present on-site at all times when work is in progress. The SSHO may also serve as the Quality Control System Manager (QCSM) but is strictly prohibited from serving as the project Superintendent. See Personnel and Contractor Qualifications. Personnel and Contractor Qualifications: To ensure technical competency and safe execution of this project, the Government requires key personnel to meet strict experience thresholds. The contractor must assign a Project Superintendent with a minimum of five (5) years of construction experience, with at least five (5) of those years acting as a superintendent on earthwork and channel restoration projects similar in size and complexity. Additionally, the contractor must provide a Quality Control System Manager (QCSM) who has a minimum of five (5) years of construction experience on similar projects and holds a valid "Construction Quality Management for Contractors" (CQM-C) certification, as well as a dedicated Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO). General Information The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The solicitation will be issued on or about 7 September 2026, via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov. The anticipated award date is 23 October 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Basis of Award is best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO 12.203(a), price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Small businesses are strongly encouraged to connect with their local APEX Accelerators to leverage these valuable services. The APEX Accelerators Website is: https://www.apexaccelerators.us/#/. The Kansas City District, United States Army Corp of Engineers (USCE), has a need for Design-Build construction services to construct a parking structure that will provide a minimum of 627 parking stalls over seven levels (6 stories) of parking at the John J. Cochran Veterans Hospital in St. Louis, MO. Each level of the structure will be approximately 35,650 square feet and support 1 additional level of parking which may be added in the future. The structure may be cast in place, or precast. The scope includes electrical and telecommunications rooms, elevators, site work, walk-ways, access points, wayfinding, and a parking space counting system. This acquisition is using FAR Subpart 36.3 Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures. In Phase 1 of the two-phase selection procedure, Offerors will submit performance capability proposals (past performance, management, staffing) demonstrating their capability to successfully execute design build construction work under the contract resulting from this solicitation. The Government will evaluate the Phase 1 proposals and intends to invite (down-select) a target of three most highly rated Phase 1 offerors to compete in Phase 2 for the design build construction contract. Offerors must submit a complete Phase 1 proposal to be considered for Phase 2. PHASE 1 DOES NOT INVOLVE A PRICING SUBMISSION. In Phase 2, a solicitation amendment will be issued to only the down-selected offerors from Phase 1, inviting them to submit a concept design solution and price proposals that conform to the Phase 2 submission, evaluation, and performance requirements. The Phase 1 D-B Request for Proposal will be available on the SAM.gov website, on or about 05 September 2026. Proposals will be due approximately 35 days later. A formal site visit and pre-proposal conference will be scheduled in Phase 2, with details provided for those in Phase II Request for Proposal. The magnitude of this design-build construction project is between $45,000,000.00 and $60,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this project is 236220-Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a Small Business Size standard of $45,000,000.00. This solicitation is being issued as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside procurement. The estimated period of performance is estimated to be about 1,007 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). Bid bond will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the offeror proposed price of $3,000,000.00, whichever is less. Performance and Payment Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. The RFP will result in the award of a single firm fixed price (FFP) design-build construction contract. Prior to bidding, vendors must be actively registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) system, and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). MITIGATION BANK CREDITS, Mississippi River and Tributaries, Mississippi River Levees Mitigation Project for Blackhawk Levee Slide Repair, Old River Seepage Berm, and Upper 5th LA Levee District Levee Enlargement Impacts to Bottomland Hardwood Habitats, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New Orleans District This will be an UNRESTRICTED procurement. All qualified business concerns may submit proposals. The New Orleans District, US Army Corps of Engineers (CEMVN), seeks to purchase Bottomland Hardwood (BLH) Wet mitigation bank credits located in the Red River Basin (Hydrologic Unit Code (HUC) 08040301). As specified below, the credits are needed to compensate for unavoidable habitat losses caused by completion of three Mississippi River Levee (MRL) projects: Blackhawk Levee Slide Repair; Old River Seepage Berm; and Upper 5th LA Levee District Levee Enlargement. As part of CEMVN�s plan to mitigate for unavoidable impacts to BLH-Wet impacts associated with the construction of the MRL projects, CEMVN will purchase BLH-Wet mitigation bank credits in the Red River Basin. The bank(s) from which credits will be purchased will be purchased through a competitive solicitation/award process. Any mitigation bank meeting the eligibility requirements and having the appropriate resource type of credits may submit a proposal to sell credits. CEMVN may enter into one or more contracts to purchase the number of credits necessary to meet CEMVN�s need at the time of purchase; however, CEMVN may purchase a lesser quantity of credits than it requires. A separate contract shall be executed for each bank credit purchase. Award will be made based on the lowest-price technically acceptable source selection process. Purchase is subject to funding availability and other USACE missions. A mitigation bank must meet all the following qualifications to be eligible to sell credits to satisfy the Mississippi River and Tributaries, Mississippi River Levees, Blackhawk Levee Slide Repair, Old River Seepage Bern, and Upper 5th LA Levee District Levee Enlargement projects mitigation requirements. For the proposal to be considered responsive and for the Offeror to be considered responsible, the mitigation bank shall: be approved by USACE and in full compliance with its Mitigation Banking Instrument (MBI), its other legal instruments (such as its conservation servitude and its financial assurances) and the standards set forth in 33 CFR Part 332; and have available Bottomland Hardwood mitigation credits within HUC 08040301; and provide the habitat type that matches the habitat type being mitigated (bottomland hardwood forest); and have mitigation credits assessed using version 1.2 of the BLH-Wet Wetland Value Assessment (WVA) Community Model available to compensate for the impacts to the particular habitat to be mitigated; and have a duly recorded perpetual conservation servitude/easement. If the Offeror fails to meet all the criteria above, the Offeror will be deemed technically unacceptable, and its offer will be considered non-responsive and ineligible for award. Habitat assessment models used for Civil Works projects are required to be certified by Headquarters, USACE Model Certification Panel and comply with the certification criteria presented in Engineer Circular EC 1105-2-412. Version 1.0 of the Wetland Value Assessment, Bottomland Hardwood Community Model has been certified. The current revision is designated Version 1.2. To facilitate the solicitation process, USACE New Orleans District, in conjunction with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, has applied Version 1.2 of the WVA Bottomland Hardwood Model to the approved banks in HUC 08040301 that possess available Bottomland Hardwood credits/acres. Credit availability is based on information provided through the USACE Regulatory In-Lieu Fee Bank Information Tracking System (RIBITS). The Wetland Value Assessment Model results will be included in the solicitation package. NAICS: 523910. A Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued on or about August 24, 2026, with a proposal due date established. Actual issue date will be shown when the solicitation is issued. The solicitation documents for this procurement will be posted on the www.SAM.gov website and can be accessed from the link located at https://www.sam.gov. You will need the Adobe Acrobat Reader for .pdf files (www.adobe.com) in order to open most files posted by the CEMVN. You are encouraged, for marketing purposes, to register as an Interested Vendor in SAM.gov. title: SmartNet CCTV/Access Systems
description: IAW RFO 5.101(c)(4): The 786th Force Support Squadron (786 FSS) at Ramstein Air Base requires Smartnet Inc. Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) and Physical Access Control System (PACS) at the Northside Fitness Center and the Vogelweh Fitness Center. This procurement allows physical access controls and real time surveillance, freeing personal from having to perform manual credential verification and preventing critical security gaps. The requirement consists of the following equipment and components: Northside Fitness Center - 28 x Hanwha Network IR Vandal Dome Cameras - 2 x Secured Door Access Assemblies (including OnGuard controllers, HID RP40 readers, and exit sensors) - Dedicated Server Infrastructure and network switching - Milestone VMS software licenses (28 camera channels) - LenelS2 OnGuard client/controller licenses - All necessary physical infrastructure materials (cabling, conduit, hardware) - Local specialized installation, testing, and configuration labor Vogelweh Fitness Center - 21 x Hanwha Network IR Vandal Dome Cameras - 1 x Secured Door Access Assembly (including OnGuard controller, HID RP40 reader, and exit sensors) - Dedicated Server Infrastructure and network switching - Milestone VMS software licenses (21 camera channels) - LenelS2 OnGuard client/controller licenses - All necessary physical infrastructure materials (cabling, conduit, hardware) Local specialized installation, testing, and configuration labor Trade Agreements Statement "One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements." Notice of Intent to Sole Source The proposed contract action is anticipated to be a sole-source acquisition to Smartnet Inc. Smartnet holds proprietary rights to the configuration data of the software and integration of the system. Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) has already centrally funded this system to be installed at the Ramstein Southside Fitness Center. Since these three locations will be configured to connect to the DAF enterprise-wide Smartnet cloud server they all need to be identical in their set and maintenance. Additionally, AFSVC currently monitors and maintains the system Authority to Operate (ATO) which encompasses all hardware and software (e.g., computer, software, monitors, door access control mechanism, cameras) which all must be strictly controlled to prevent vulnerabilities from being introduced into the cloud-based system. Notwithstanding this, all responsible sources may submit a statement of capability, quotation, bid, or proposal, which will be considered by the agency. An offeror�s proposed equipment and support must meet the requirements listed above to be eligible for potential award. If no eligible responses are received, the award will be made to Smartnet Inc. This acquisition is subject to the availability of FY26 O&M funds, with the anticipated contract award date currently TBD pending the securing of necessary funding.

title: Upphandling av två spånsugar för inomhusbruk, varav en med integrerad brikettmaskin samt rörplaneringsarbete
description: Upphandling av två spånsugar för inomhusbruk, varav en med integrerad brikettmaskin samt rörplaneringsarbete Optima samkommun (beställare/upphandlingsenhet) begär anbud på två (2) spånsugar varav den större med integrerad brikettmaskin, inom budgetanslaget, enligt denna anbudsförfrågan och dess bilagor. I anbudet ingår även planering för omändring av befintligt rörsystem. Den större spånsugen med integrerad brikettmaskin placeras i utrymmet för artesanutbildning. Den mindre spånsugen placeras i utrymmet för byggutbildningen. I anbudet ska ingå två st. olika spånsugar för inomhusbruk, varav den större med integrerad brikettmaskin, rörplaneringsarbete, leverans, montering, provkörning och användarutbildning. Optima monterar bort befintlig spånsug och utför ändringsarbetet på befintligt rörsystem.,

Muutot toteutetaan pääasiassa Kainuun hyvinvointialueen alueella, palveluyksiköiden tai Kainuun hyvinvointialueen osoittamien yksittäisten asiakkaiden muuttotarpeiden mukaisesti. Tilaaja pidättää oikeuden ilman uutta kilpailutusta tehdä hankintapäätöksen ja hankintasopimuksen toiseksi tulleen palveluntuottajan kanssa, mikäli voittaneen palveluntuottajan kanssa ei päästä sopimukseen.,

This code is used when the Government did not initially purchase the data and/or rights. The Government does not own or have access to the data for these items. No samples are available for potential suppliers to evaluate. The Government did not provision for a competitive acquisition package including the full repair technical data or acquisition of any test equipment that would be required to perform organic repairs. title: Germany – Ticket-validation machines – Markterkundung Showcase Validatoren
description: 1. Auftraggeber: Die Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe (BVG), Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts, sind der federführende Anbieter von ÖPNV-Dienstleistungen im Ballungsraum Berlin. 2. Bezeichnung des Auftrags durch den öffentlichen Auftraggeber: Kauf von Dummy Validatoren zu Vorführzwecken durch den Bereich Vertrieb und Marketing. 3. Kurze Beschreibung der Art der Dienstleistungen: In anderen Ländern - und mittlerweile auch schon in einigen Pilotregionen in Deutschland - sind ID-basierte Vertriebskonzepte erfolgreich im Einsatz. Bei diesen innovativen Ansätzen für den Verkauf von Fahrtberechtigungen wird der bestehende Prozess komplett umgekehrt. title: Germany – Health services – Evaluation des Sofortprogramms Cybersicherheit
description: Aufgrund der hohen Gefährdungslage im Cyberraum hat der Bundesgesetzgeber ein Sofortprogramm Cybersicherheit zum Schutz der akutstationären Versorgung im Bundeshaushalt verankert. Das Förderprogramm soll systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen entlang der kritischen (Akut-)Versorgungskette die erforderlichen Ressourcen für moderne Schutzmaßnahmen bereitstellen und gleichzeitig zur Erfüllung der verpflichtenden NIS-2-Richtlinie beitragen. Die eingesetzten IT-Systeme werden damit sowohl präventiv vor Angriffen geschützt, als auch in die Lage versetzt, bei Sicherheitsvorfällen schnell wieder in einen funktionsfähigen Zustand zu gelangen. Dies gewährleistet eine durchgehende Akutversorgung im Krisenfall. Im Zuge des Sofortprogrammes Cybersicherheit soll der Digitalisierungsgrad insgesamt und im Besonderen der IT-Sicherheitsgrad der systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen entlang der kritischen Versorgungskette erfasst werden (vgl. Modul 1 zur weiteren Erläuterung). Anhand auf anerkannten Reifegradmodellen basierender und noch festzulegender Kriterien sollen systemrelevante Gesundheitseinrichtungen im Rahmen einer Selbsteinschätzung eine Einstufung und Bewertung ihres IT-Sicherheits- und Digitalisierungsstands vornehmen. Die Teilnahme an der Selbsteinschätzung ist verpflichtend für Einrichtungen, die im Rahmen des Sofortprogrammes eine Förderung erhalten. Grundsätzlich soll die Teilnahme allerdings sämtlichen berechtigten systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen entlang der kritischen Versorgungskette offenstehen. Die Daten werden im Anschluss aggregiert ausgewertet. Es sind drei Erhebungszeiträume in den Jahren 2027, 2028 und 2029 vorgesehen. Die erste Erhebung soll im Jahr 2027 stattfinden und anschließend im jährlichen Turnus fortgeführt werden, mit weiteren Erhebungen in den Jahren 2028 und 2029. Innerhalb dieser Erhebungszeiträume können die konkreten Erhebungszeitpunkte für die jeweiligen Einrichtungsgruppen unter Berücksichtigung der bestehenden Datenlage und des jeweiligen Erkenntnisbedarfs zeitlich differenziert festgelegt werden. Insbesondere kann die erste Erhebung bei den weiteren systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen, für die bislang keine vergleichbare Datengrundlage vorliegt, zu einem früheren Zeitpunkt erfolgen. Für den Krankenhausbereich kann demgegenüber auf bereits vorliegende Erkenntnisse aus der jüngsten Erhebung des DigitalRadar aufgebaut und die nächste Erhebung entsprechend zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt durchgeführt werden. Einerseits kann so der Status Quo der systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen zu den drei Messzeitpunkten erfasst werden, andererseits kann durch den Vergleich der drei Messzeitpunkte ein längsschnittlicher Verlauf abgebildet werden. Dieser ermöglicht die Bewertung, inwieweit die Digitalisierung/IT-Sicherheit der systemrelevanten Gesundheitseinrichtungen im Rahmen des Sofortprogramms verbessert werden konnte. Auf dieser Grundlage können zudem Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung moderner Sicherheitsvorkehrungen, zur Erfüllung der Anforderungen der NIS-2-Richtlinie, zur Stärkung der Resilienz und Versorgungssicherheit sowie zur Optimierung des Ressourceneinsatzes bewertet werden. Die Details entnehmen Sie bitte den Vergabeunterlagen.

description: The contract for services will be awarded in the form of the NHS Standard Sub-contract. This Service is for the provision of an Intensive and Assertive Outreach (I&A) Service across Norfolk and Suffolk. The Service is designed to deliver intensive, proactive, and flexible community-based care for individuals with Serious Mental Illness (SMI) who present with elevated levels of complexity and risk and for whom engagement with traditional mental health services is a challenge. Delivery will be through a blended model between Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust (NSFT) as the Head Provider and Sub-Contractors (encouraging Voluntary, Community, Faith, and Social Enterprise (VCFSE) interest), ensuring a comprehensive offer that integrates clinical expertise with community-based engagement and recovery support. The Sub-Contractor will play a critical role in enabling engagement, promoting recovery, and addressing the wider determinants of health, working as a fully integrated partner alongside NSFT clinical teams. The Sub-Contractor(s) contribution is central to achieving the core ambition of the service: No individual is excluded from care due to disengagement, complexity, or social circumstances. Assertive Engagement and Outreach The Sub-Contractor must: • Deliver proactive, persistent outreach, particularly where individuals are disengaged • Provide frequent contact, including daily visits in line with the care plan • Engage individuals in a variety of settings, including: - Their home - Community settings - Places where they feel safe - In-reaching into hospitals or prisons if required to establish engagement and promote continuity of care • Use creative and flexible engagement approaches, including: - Doorstep engagement - Accompaniment to appointments - Informal relational contact - Demonstrate the ability to sustain engagement over extended periods, particularly where trust is low The sub-contractor(s) will provide: • Assertive Engagement and Outreach • Practical Support for Daily Living • Community Participation and Social Inclusion • Support to Access Healthcare (Including Mental Health Care) • Medication Support (Non-Clinical) • Substance Misuse and Harm Reduction • Carer and Family Support • Contribution to Risk Management Sub-Contractors will work mainly in the Community travelling to Service Users and must demonstrate their ability to deliver outreach across urban, rural and coastal communities, including service users placed outside their immediate locality. The service would be well suited for providers in the Voluntary, Community, Faith, and Social Enterprise sector. The full service specification, along with the full set of procurement documents, is available upon request by contacting ContractsTeam@nsft.nhs.uk

title: Finland – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – An Anechoic Radio Frequency (RF) Chamber
description: Tampere University (thereinafter also "TAU" or "Contracting Authority" calls for tenders for an Anechoic Radio Frequency (RF) Chamber for Hervanta Campus' Sähkötalo. The procurement concerns an Anechoic RF Chamer (hereinafter referred to as "Chamber") for wireless communication technology, to be integrated into the WICO research environment and primarily used by the Tampere Wireless Research Center. The facility will be used for conducting Over-The-Air (OTA) antenna measurements, supporting advanced research and experimental validation in wireless communications. The chamber will enable research on current and future wireless systems and will further strengthen the existing high-level research in the field. The object of the tender process is described in more detail in the invitation to tender documents. A dedicated space has been allocated for both the chamber and an adjacent control room. Detailed layouts and spatial specifications are provided in the appendices to this tender. In addition, a separate appendix outlines the existing measurement equipment that will be installed and utilized within the new chamber. The chamber will be constructed within the Sähkötalo building, in the F-wing. The chamber is effectively located at the ground-floor level, allowing convenient access through large doors. This facilitates the transportation and installation of sizeable chamber components and measurement equipment. The selected supplier will be required to conduct a site survey promptly after contract signing. The purpose of the survey is to verify all relevant dimensions, environmental conditions, and technical details necessary for the design and installation of the chamber. Access to the site during the renovation phase will require coordination with the main construction contractor (details are provided after the contract has been signed). It is expected that participation in a mandatory construction site safety training (approximately one hour) will be required prior to site access. At the time of issuing this tender, the specified area within Sähkötalo is undergoing renovation. The renovation is scheduled for completion by the end of April 2027. Consequently, construction of the anechoic chamber is expected to commence at the beginning May 2027, subject to the completion of renovation works and in the absence of unforeseen delays. The anticipated construction period for the chamber is during spring-summer 2027. Budget Available: Please note maximum budget available for this procurement is no greater than 500.000 € (EUR, excl. VAT).
